newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela to visit Middle East in November.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela to visit Middle East in November.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela will pay his first visit to the Middle East in November with a tour that includes Israel and Palestinian territories, his office said on Monday.

"From November 4 he will travel to Israel, Palestine, Jordan and Egypt. He'll meet all the leaders but the dates for the length of his stay are not yet finalised," presidential office spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters.
Mandela has twice postponed scheduled visits to Israel, first planned for August and then October.
Mankahlana said the delays were to accommodate a lengthier stay in the Middle East, as this would be Mandela's first trip to the region.
The South African president is to meet both Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Mandela's ruling African National Congress (ANC) for decades identified with the PLO, Israel's former arch-foe led by Arafat, while the ANC struggled against white-led South African rule.
Israel officially opposed apartheid. But facing world criticism over its treatment of Palestinians, Israel shared a sense of isolation with South Africa.
Israel's groundbreaking peace deal with the PLO in 1993 coincided with the scrapping of apartheid rule, paving the way for a thaw in relations between the ANC and the Jewish state.
South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo visited Israel last September and declared a desire to forge strong ties.
Trade in non-military goods with Israel totalled 2.25 billion rand ($459 million) in 1995, up from $370 million in 1994.

The South African Foreign Trade Organisation said Israeli exports to South Africa were worth 985 million rand in 1995, 62 percent more than the year before. South African exports to Israel rose 19 percent in the same period to 1.27 billion rand.
